content.text:
All three sizes are rendered and verified. **Output** (in the working folder): | File | Size | Layout | |---|---|---| | `square.png` | 1080×1080 | Logo header, speaker row (circle + name/role), title block, footer with date + button | | `landscape.png` | 1920×1080 | Two columns — title left, large portrait with name/role right; date and button anchored bottom | | `story.png` | 1080×1920 | Fully centered vertical stack, 420px portrait as the hero | **Design:** `#0F1226` base with violet radial glows and a faint masked grid; Inter loaded via `@font-face` from the local variable TTF (weights 500/600/700 all exercised). Portrait is a `background-size: cover` div with `aspect-ratio: 1/1` and a violet ring, so it stays perfectly circular at every scale. The title carries a violet "Keynote" kicker and sets in 3 balanced lines at all three sizes (57/70/64px). **Verification:** rather than eyeballing alone, I wrote `check.js`, which loads each page at its exact viewport and asserts: - no element extends past the viewport on any edge - `scrollWidth/scrollHeight` never exceed the canvas (no hidden overflow) - no clipping inside any element that actually clips - zero pairwise bounding-box overlap across all 9 text/visual elements - the portrait is measurably square (148/352/420px, width == height) First run caught two issues, which I fixed: the landscape role was being force-broken onto two lines by a `
` that was no longer needed once I widened that column, and the square had a disconnected dead band between the speaker row and the title, fixed by grouping them into one block so the whitespace distributes evenly. Final run: all three pass.
